headline:
Firm on who,
loose on how.
intro: I keep one map of the team: what each person owns, what they’re the go-to for, and where they want to grow next. Who takes which work, who helps whom, and what we ask the business to fund all come from it.
Each person gets growth they chose, the team solves most problems without me, and the company gets a design group that’s easy to plan around.

levels.label: Person
levels.imageAlt: A person node has two attached tags for a product and a specialty, with an arrow leaving the map in the direction they want to grow.

principles.headline:
One product,
one specialty.
principles.body: Each designer owns a product’s design and research, and is the team’s go-to for one specialty. Everyone knows who to ask and what they own.

principles.headline:
Goals they wrote,
tied to yours.
principles.body: Each quarter we write personal goals against what the business needs. I assign work to match, so growth and delivery follow the same plan.

principles.headline:
I coach judgment,
not process.
principles.body: Our 1:1s work on reading a room, saying “not yet,” and choosing the next move when a partner is stuck. Each team needs different judgment.

levels.label: Team
levels.imageAlt: Six peer nodes carry ownership tags and pass work to neighboring nodes through arrows, with no central manager node.

principles.headline:
Problems route
sideways first.
principles.body: Specialties help the team answer most questions together. That keeps me out of the critical path and makes it clear who the senior people are.

principles.headline:
The team owns
the quality bar.
principles.body: A weekly roundtable and design review decides what we improve and who leads it, so standards hold whether or not I’m in the room.

principles.headline:
Stuck work gets a
second pair of hands.
principles.body: When something stalls I work alongside the designer. They keep ownership of the project, build their judgment, and need less of me the next time.

levels.label: Company
levels.imageAlt: A request enters a sheet of six products, with four attached designer nodes and two tally marks counting products without a designer.

principles.headline:
Talk before it
becomes a ticket.
principles.body: Every request starts with a conversation about the outcome, what each team needs, and the dates involved. That gives you timelines you can plan around.

principles.headline:
Cover the gap
and count it.
principles.body: Products without a designer get what we can give. I track what that costs and use the count to build the headcount case I bring you.

principles.headline:
Team shape is
a design decision.
principles.body: Structure changes retention and work quality, so I’d design it for your company and expect it to look different from the last one.

closing: The map is the one constant. Each company gets its own version, and the work changes with it.
